thesis: Lumentum is the sharpest growth story in AI optics right now: Q3 FY2026 revenue $808.4M (+90% y/y) with non-GAAP operating margin exploding to 32.2% (+2,140bps y/y), Q4 guided to $960M-$1.01B and EPS $2.85-$3.05. The company is sold out, under-shipping demand by ~30% even after ~40% capacity expansion, with OCS backlog above $400M and an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar CPO order for 1H CY2027. The stock has re-rated violently to reflect this (+121% over 12 months to ~$728, ~$57B cap), leaving execution perfection embedded in the price, and the balance sheet carries meaningful debt with tight current ratios.
catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results (August 2026): guidance $960M-$1.01B revenue, non-GAAP OM 35-36%, EPS $2.85-$3.05
OCS (optical circuit switch) scaling - backlog already above $400M
Incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar CPO order deliverable 1H calendar 2027
Further capacity expansion converting the ~30% under-shipped demand into revenue
Continued laser-chip/transceiver design wins in AI datacenter build-outs
risk_factors: Valuation: ~$57B cap prices years of continued hypergrowth; at ~61x annualized forward EPS a single guide-down resets the multiple hard
Balance sheet: debt is meaningful and current ratios are tight; management raised preferred stock and pushed out maturities to buy room
AI-capex concentration: demand is hyperscaler-driven and cyclical; 'sold out' can become 'inventory correction' within two quarters (optics history)
Competitive intensity: Coherent, InnoLight, and in-house hyperscaler optics programs target the same sockets
CPO transition could cannibalize pluggable transceivers faster than OCS/CPO revenue replaces them
